subject: smartphone screen
title: What If You Never Cleaned Your Phone?

scenes.text: What if you never wiped your phone? One scientist says a toilet seat is cleaner.
A 2016 study found the average user touched their phone about two thousand six hundred times a day.
Swabs from students' phones found more than seventeen thousand bacterial gene copies per phone.
A University of Arizona estimate put phones at about ten times the bacteria of most toilet seats, because toilets get cleaned.
In a 2025 study, two in three people used their phone on the toilet, and they stayed far longer.
The twist: most of those germs are your own. The real risk starts when you hand your phone to someone else.

description:
What if you never cleaned your phone? A 2016 dscout study counted about 2,617 phone touches a day per user, and a study of high-school students' phones found over 17,000 bacterial gene copies per phone. University of Arizona microbiologist Charles Gerba estimated phones carry about 10 times more bacteria than most toilet seats.
In a 2025 PLOS One study, 66% of adults used their phone on the toilet and were far more likely to stay over five minutes. Experts say most phone bacteria are your own; sharing phones is the bigger risk.
